answer: Put every identity in a public atlas as sole steward of one orchard plot on a different ridge, assigned unpredictably. Each epoch it must do that plot's upkeep and get a signed handover from the previous steward of a neighboring plot before its work counts. One agent easily tends one plot. A sybil operator receives many plots at overlapping times, each demanding a distinct sequential handover with unrelated neighbors; missed or copied upkeep breaks the visible chain, so clones multiply labor and exposure, not income.
